newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk MP urges trial of anti-Islamist general.
newsitem.headline: Turk MP urges trial of anti-Islamist general.

text.p: An MP from Turkey's ruling Welfare Party called in comments published on Monday for a court martial to try a leading member of the secularist military for making anti-Islamist comments.

The Milliyet daily quoted deputy Siddik Altay as saying General Cevik Bir, the armed forces' second-in-command, made an "undemocratic" speech at a Turkish association meeting in the United States last week.
"If I had the authority I would immediately suspend that general, try him in a court martial and discharge him from the army," Altay said.
Bir was reported by the Turkish media to have vowed in his speech that the army would not permit Islamists to change NATO member Turkey's strictly secular system.
Tension between the Islamist wing of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's coalition and the generals has risen amid growing debate on secularism in recent weeks.

Tanks paraded on the streets of the central town of Sincan this month after the Welfare town council organised anti-Israel protests. The tanks' presence was seen as a warning to Welfare not to encourage Islamist militants.

Bir, who headed U.N. forces in Somalia in 1994, was also quoted as describing Turkey's neighbour Iran as a "terrorist state". Ankara often accuses Tehran of backing Kurdish rebels fighting in southeast Turkey.
